undated_mentions: 1926–27 District Championships I: runners-up
1943–44 Cupa Eroilor participation (wartime cup)
1948–49 season: played as CSU Timișoara
1957–58 Romanian Cup win (1–0 vs Progresul București)
1957–58 season: joint first in league, lost on goal difference
late 1960s: struggle to remain in the first league
1973–74 Romanian Cup final lost
1978 league third place under Angelo Niculescu
1978–79 UEFA Cup: beat MTK Budapest, lost to Honvéd in second round
1979–80 Romanian Cup win (2–1 vs Steaua București)
1980–81 Cup Winners' Cup: beat Celtic, lost to West Ham United
1981–82 Cup Winners' Cup: lost to Leipzig on aggregate
1983–89 yo-yo between Divizia A and Divizia B (ABBA years)
1990–91 UEFA Cup: beat Atlético Madrid
1991–92 season: 5th place; Romanian Cup final lost on penalties to Steaua
1992–93 UEFA Cup: 1–1 vs Real Madrid, lost 0–4 away
1996–97 season: relegated again
1999–2000 season (approx.): 15th place, relegated to Divizia C
Dacia Pitești licence purchase to play in Divizia B (date not stated)
2001–02 season: last place, negative eight points, relegated
2001–02 season: Claudio Zambon departure after disputes with local authorities
2002–03 season: relegation play-off survived vs Gloria Buzău
2004–05 season: renamed FCU Politehnica Timișoara
Takeover by Balkan Petroleum Ltd. (Marian Iancu), date not stated
Renamed FC Timișoara after Court of Arbitration for Sport decision (date not stated)
2007–08 season: UEFA Cup qualification
2008–09 season: Liga I runners-up; Romanian Cup runners-up
2009–10 season: UEFA Champions League third qualifying round; Europa League group stage
2010–11 season: Liga I runners-up, then relegated to Liga II after licence refusal
2011–12 season: Liga II winners, licence refused
Bankruptcy filing after 2011–12 season (date not stated)
2015–16 season: returned to white-purple colours
2016–17 season: 14-point penalty; beat UTA Arad 5–2 in relegation play-off; Cupa Ligii runners-up; Romanian Cup semi-finals
2017–18 season: relegated on last matchday
2018–19 Liga 2 season: insolvency declared; relocated to Electrica stadium
Liga II runners-up: 1970–71, 2012–13
Cupa Ligii runners-up: 2016–17
Liga I runners-up: 2008–09, 2010–11
